title: Make the prompt-skew and enter-worktree path tests hold on Windows
action: Tests only; never change product code. (1) verbs/drivers/tests.rs, test prompt_skew_names_the_offending_file_and_its_remedy (~line 4739): on Windows the message prints `.bee\bin\prompts\gather.md`, so `msg.contains(".bee/bin/prompts/gather.md")` fails. Compare against `msg.replace('\\', "/")` for the path check (keep the other assertions as they are). (2) verbs/worktree/tests.rs, test enter_worktree_core_verifies_grant_and_git_link_with_zero_mutation (~line 5987): result["worktreeRoot"] is the git-reported long path (C:\\Users\\runneradmin\\...) while created.worktree_root is the temp-dir 8.3 short path (C:\\Users\\RUNNER~1\\...). Compare `dunce::canonicalize` of both paths (the crate already depends on dunce) instead of the raw strings; check the same test for any other raw-path string compare of the same pair and treat it the same way. Run `cargo test --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee prompt_skew` and `... enter_worktree_core` — green on Linux. One commit, subject in imperative mood, trailer `cell: wtp-2`.
verify: cargo test --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee prompt_skew && cargo test --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee enter_worktree_core

truths: Both tests pass on Linux and no longer depend on the path separator or on the short/long form of a Windows path
prohibitions: No change to any non-test source file

trace.outcome: prompt-skew path check is separator-neutral (verbs/drivers/tests.rs:4739); enter-worktree compares dunce-canonical paths (verbs/worktree/tests.rs:5987) and the text check reuses the printed worktreeRoot

report.outcome: prompt-skew and enter-worktree path tests no longer depend on the path separator or the 8.3 short form of a Windows path
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee — green:unit — full bee bin suite in CI release mode on Linux, run by the leader after both cells landed; Windows-only behavior is proven by the Windows CI run after merge
